newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-Costello says Australian economy is on track.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says Australian economy is on track.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello has moved to quell growing investor concerns about the government's economic growth projections.

Speaking via satellite to the McIntosh Securities Investment Conference in New York, Costello played down "softness" in recent employment advertisement figures, reassuring the audience of fund managers and analysts that the government would meet its forecast for 1.5 percent employment growth for the year to June.
"It can be principally explained by the decline in advertising in relation to the public sector job advertisements," Costello said.

The Treasurer said the government-instigated two percent cut in Commonwealth public service operating costs had resulted in the decline and he remained confident healthy business investment growth of 14 percent and a generally supportive world economy would help the government meet budget goals.
"I think our 3.5 percent growth forecast is pretty good. It's probably in the middle of the range," Costello said.

Earlier, Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd chief executive John Prescott gave a resounding vote of confidence in the government's policies and echoed most of its predictions during a luncheon address to the McIntosh conference.
He assured the conference that the government's push for industrial reform would eventually led to increases in productivity to help boost employment.
During a question and answer session after his address to the conference, Costello said he was confident the government's industrial reform package would make it through the Senate.
"I must say to you we think prospects are good in the Senate, we always have to argue our case, we don't take any votes for granted and we negotiate all the time with all the parties," Costello said.
"We are only two votes short on any issue ... and I think we have a lot of moral-suasion on this issue," he said.
